newsitem.title: USA: Penn. Rep. Shuster under investigation - report.
newsitem.headline: Penn. Rep. Shuster under investigation - report.

text.p: Pennsylvania Congressman E.G. "Bud" Shuster is under investigation by a federal grand jury in Boston over whether he used his influence to aid two Boston businessmen, the Boston Globe reported Monday.

The grand jury is focusing on what influence Shuster, Republican chairman of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, and his former top aide may have used to aid the two businessmen, who contributed to Shuster's political committee, the newspaper said.

The Globe said that sources familiar with the probe said the U.S. attorney's office in Boston several weeks ago delivered grand jury subpoenas to the project office of the $7.78 billion Central Artery or "Big Dig" highway project in downtown Boston.

The subpoenas, also sent to the state agency Massachusetts Port Authority, sought all correspondence the agencies had with the Pennsylvania Republican and his former aide, Ann Eppard, now a Washington lobbyist.
The apparent focus of the probe is whether Shuster or Eppard used their positions to win the two businessmen favourable settlements in disputes involving the Big Dig over land, the Globe said.
The U.S. Attorney's office in Boston declined to confirm or deny the existence of an investigation.

Both of the businessmen, Richard Goldberg and Nicholas Contos, were major contributors to Shuster's campaign committee, the newspaper said. Goldberg gave $6,000 between 1991 and 1993 and Contos gave $4,500 between 1991 and 1995, the newspaper said.
